class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Limit Process", [
            "Zoom in on the curve.",
            "Move two points closer together.",
            "Secant line becomes a tangent line."
        ])
        
        # Setup graph elements
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 3], y_range=[-1, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, color=BLUE)
        
        # Grid area for plot
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        axes.shift(RIGHT * 1.5)
        curve.move_to(axes.c2p(1, 1)) # Center curve on axes
        
        p1 = Dot(axes.c2p(1, 1), color=YELLOW)
        p2_tracker = ValueTracker(2)
        p2 = always_redraw(lambda: Dot(axes.c2p(p2_tracker.get_value(), p2_tracker.get_value()**2), color=RED))
        
        secant = always_redraw(lambda: Line(
            p1.get_center(), p2.get_center(), color=RED, stroke_width=3
        ))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), Create(curve), FadeIn(p1), FadeIn(p2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)
        self.add(secant)
        self.play(p2_tracker.animate.set_value(1.1), run_time=2)
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GRAY)
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)
        tangent = Line(axes.c2p(0, -1), axes.c2p(2, 3), color=GREEN, stroke_width=3)
        self.play(
            FadeOut(secant),
            FadeOut(p2),
            Create(tangent),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivative is the limit of change.",
            "Formalize as a difference quotient.",
            "Limit as h approaches zero.",
            "Connect to tangent line slope.",
            "Calculates instantaneous rate of change."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Derivative", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        formula = MathTex(r"f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}", font_size=40)
        limit_notation = formula[0][7:14] # "lim_{h \to 0}" part

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)))
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)))
        # B018: Highlight limit notation
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color(WHITE), limit_notation.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[3].set_opacity(1)))
        # Draw a small indicator for h shrinking
        h_indicator = VGroup(
            Dot(color=RED).move_to(self.grid["E3"]),
            Arrow(start=self.grid["E3"], end=self.grid["E5"], color=RED)
        )
        self.play(Create(h_indicator))
        self.play(h_indicator.animate.scale(0.5).fade(0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[4].set_opacity(1)))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Instantaneous Velocity", [
            "Apply to drone motion.", 
            "Position's derivative is velocity.", 
            "Find exact speed at 2s."
        ])
        
        # Persistent objects
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5, 1], y_range=[0, 10, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True})
        func = lambda t: 0.5 * t**2
        graph = axes.plot(func, color=BLUE)
        
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "B2", scale_factor=0.4)
        self.place_at_grid(graph, "B2", scale_factor=0.4)
        
        tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        
        def get_point():
            x = tracker.get_value()
            return axes.c2p(x, func(x))
        
        point.add_updater(lambda p: p.move_to(get_point()))
        self.add(point)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(axes), Create(graph))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        tangent_line = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=RED)
        
        def get_slope():
            x = tracker.get_value()
            return func(x + 0.01) - func(x)
            
        tangent_line.add_updater(lambda l: l.set_angle(np.arctan(tracker.get_value())).move_to(point.get_center()))
        self.add(tangent_line)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.play(tracker.animate.set_value(2), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: Prerequisite: Average Speed vs. Instantaneous Speed
sections.content: Define average rate of change as the slope of a secant line between two points. Use a visual of a Cheetah running to explain that speed varies over time, leading to the need for a more precise measurement at a single moment.
sections.example: A Cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds; its average speed is 20 m/s, but its speedometer fluctuated during the sprint.

sections.title: Visualizing the Limit Process
sections.content: Introduce the 'Zoom-in' effect. Show the secant line between two points on a curve. Gradually bring the two points closer together (Δx → 0). Visually transform the secant line into a tangent line.
sections.example: An animation showing two points on a parabolic path (f(x)=x²) getting infinitely close until the secant line snaps into the tangent line at a specific point.

sections.title: Defining the Derivative
sections.content: Formally define the derivative as the limit of the difference quotient: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Connect this directly to the slope of the tangent line at point x.
sections.example: Algebraic derivation for f(x) = x², showing the resulting slope formula is 2x.

sections.title: Application: The Instantaneous Velocity
sections.content: Apply the concept to motion. If position is s(t), the derivative s'(t) gives the instantaneous velocity. This demonstrates the practical utility of derivatives in physics.
sections.example: A drone taking off; use the derivative of its height function to calculate its exact velocity at the 2-second mark.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap that the derivative is simply the 'slope function.' Emphasize that it captures 'instantaneous change' by taking the limit as the interval of change shrinks to zero.
sections.example: A final infographic showing: Secant (Average) -> Tangent (Instantaneous) -> Derivative.
